topic_summary: Analysis of Vatican II (1962-65) as a composite doctrinal shift rather than a single reinterpretation. The Council issued 16 documents across multiple domains (liturgy, ecclesiology, ecumenism, religious freedom) through contested processes between progressive and conservative factions, generating competing hermeneutics that remain unresolved in post-conciliar implementation.

key_entities: Pope John XXIII (convener, aggiornamento vision, died 1963)
Progressive faction (Cardinals Bea, Frings; theologians Congar, periti)
Conservative faction (Cardinals Ottaviani, Siri, Ruffini; Coetus Internationalis Patrum)
Society of Saint Pius X (SSPX, largest traditionalist rejection group)
Pope Benedict XVI (post-conciliar hermeneutic of continuity advocate)
key_tensions: Progressive vs Conservative factions (competing visions of Church reform)
Curia vs Bishops (administrative control vs episcopal collegiality)
Continuity vs Rupture hermeneutics (organic development vs substantive break)
Letter vs Spirit (document text vs post-conciliar implementation)
Doctrinal development vs stability (Newman's influence vs traditional fixity)
Validity acceptance vs rejection (mainstream vs SSPX traditionalists)
key_claims: Vatican II was aggiornamento (updating) not rupture (John XXIII, Paul VI, Benedict XVI)
Vatican II was riddled with ambiguities from factional compromise (traditionalist view)
Post-conciliar implementation exceeded/contradicted documents (Latin elimination, liturgical experimentation)
Multiple distinct doctrinal shifts occurred simultaneously (religious freedom, collegiality, ecumenism, liturgy, lay ministry)
10-12% of Fathers rejected three key documents on theological grounds (significant internal disagreement)
Vatican II is invalid due to doctrinal conflict with established teaching (SSPX position)
key_mechanisms: Factional compromise producing ambiguous texts (progressive-conservative negotiation)
Post-conciliar interpretive spin (appeal to 'spirit of Vatican II' vs document letter)
Curia resistance then progressive implementation (initial draft rejection, subsequent reform)
Hermeneutic selection (continuity vs rupture frameworks applied retroactively)
key_absences: Formal mechanism for resolving hermeneutic disputes (no authoritative post-conciliar interpretation body)
Enforcement mechanism for document fidelity (Latin preservation mandate ignored)
Theological reconciliation of contradictory positions (religious freedom vs traditional teaching on error having no rights)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Vatican II as authoritative doctrinal event: 16 conciliar documents claiming continuity with Catholic tradition while introducing substantive reforms across liturgy, ecclesiology, ecumenism, and religious freedom
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Papal and episcopal magisterium claiming interpretive authority through apostolic succession and conciliar consensus, grounded in claim of organic doctrinal development under Holy Spirit guidance

readings.commitment: Vatican II represents organic doctrinal development in continuity with tradition; reforms are legitimate expressions of unchanging deposit of faith
readings.authority_grounding: Papal magisterium (Benedict XVI), appeal to Newman's development theory, claim of Holy Spirit guidance ensuring continuity
readings.expected_structural_delta: All 16 documents valid; post-conciliar reforms legitimate when faithful to texts; ambiguities resolvable through traditional hermeneutics; beneficiary: progressive reformers claiming continuity; victim: none (reforms are cost-free development)

readings.commitment: Vatican II represents substantive break with tradition; documents contain doctrinal errors or irreconcilable contradictions with prior teaching
readings.authority_grounding: Traditional magisterium (pre-Vatican II papal teaching), claim that error has no rights (religious freedom contradiction), liturgical tradition (Latin mandate)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Council invalid or gravely defective; post-conciliar Church in crisis; beneficiary: modernist faction; victim: traditional Catholic identity and doctrinal stability; SSPX position instantiates this reading

readings.commitment: Vatican II is not a single interpretable event but an overdetermined composite of multiple distinct doctrinal shifts with incompatible theological rationales, producing structural ambiguity that cannot be resolved into either continuity or rupture
readings.authority_grounding: Sociological observation of factional compromise, empirical evidence of divergent implementations, recognition that 10-12% rejection rates on key documents indicate unresolved theological conflict
readings.expected_structural_delta: Neither continuity nor rupture framework captures reality; ambiguities are not resolvable because they encode genuine theological contradictions from factional compromise; beneficiary: scholars recognizing complexity; victim: institutional authority claiming univocal interpretation; post-conciliar conflicts are structural not accidental

axiom_contradictions.basis: Continuity reading requires accepting that doctrinal development can introduce substantive novelty (religious freedom as human right) while remaining in continuity with tradition that denied it; rupture reading requires accepting that ecumenical council under papal authority can err doctrinally. No single framework holds both: either councils can develop doctrine organically (continuity) or they cannot introduce novelty without rupture (rupture).

Composite reading requires accepting that Vatican II's ambiguities encode irresolvable theological contradictions from factional compromise; continuity reading requires accepting that all ambiguities are resolvable through traditional hermeneutics under Holy Spirit guidance. No single framework holds both: either the Council produced genuinely contradictory outputs (composite) or all outputs are harmonizable (continuity).

Composite reading treats Vatican II as structurally ambiguous event requiring sociological analysis of factional dynamics; rupture reading treats it as failed doctrinal event requiring theological judgment of validity. While both reject simple continuity, composite denies the possibility of univocal theological judgment that rupture requires. No single framework holds both: either the event is too complex for binary validity judgment (composite) or validity is the primary question (rupture).

omegas.description: No formal mechanism exists for resolving hermeneutic disputes or enforcing document fidelity (Latin mandate ignored). Is this absence a feature (allowing adaptive interpretation) or a bug (enabling drift)? If feature, continuity reading becomes piton of claimed authority without enforcement. If bug, composite reading gains support.

Continuity reading grounds authority in Holy Spirit guidance ensuring doctrinal development remains in continuity. This claim is empirically untestable and theologically contested. If accepted, continuity reading is rope. If rejected, becomes tangled_rope of authority claim without verification mechanism.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + commitment_system_recognition authority_grounding

omegas.description: SSPX recognizes papal authority but rejects Vatican II validity. Is this coherent (papal authority separable from conciliar authority) or incoherent (papal authority includes ratifying councils)? Resolution affects whether rupture reading is internally consistent or self-contradictory.

Composite overdetermination reading describes Vatican II as structurally ambiguous but does not specify normative response. Does recognizing irreducible ambiguity require abandoning univocal interpretation (victim: institutional authority) or does it enable pragmatic pluralism (beneficiary: diverse implementations)? Epsilon bin may shift based on normative framing.
omegas.source: composite_overdetermination_reading victim field + Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium)

omegas.description: 10-12% Father rejection rates on three key documents cited as evidence of unresolved theological conflict. What threshold constitutes 'significant disagreement' vs 'normal minority dissent'? If 10-12% is normal, weakens composite reading. If abnormally high, strengthens it. No baseline comparison provided.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel/reading decomposition applied per §1.3-K. Three readings selected represent genuinely distinct interpretive commitments with mutually exclusive axioms. Composite overdetermination reading is structurally novel (not standard in theological literature) but grounded in empirical evidence of factional compromise and divergent implementations. Deferred axes capture mechanisms and consequences without redundancy.
